answer: Before taking a voyage-planning, tundra-survey or nebula-imaging job, each key must finish a verifiable delay function on H(epoch beacon, key). Validators check the succinct proof and reject late or invalid tickets. T sequential squarings cost each extra alias a fresh chain; changing the key changes the input, preventing replay. Many aliases can run in parallel, but need roughly nT total squarings and enough hardware to meet the same deadline. Security assumes unpredictable beacons and no shortcut to sequential evaluation; faster hardware still helps.
